title: Candidate governed System/Solution Architecture
purpose: Describe the candidate system boundary, exact interactions, quality attributes, decisions, and conformance expectations for accountable review.

included: Governed engine, Product Studio host, and workspace store boundary
excluded: Provider execution, release topology, and production deployment
boundaries: Candidate design only with no approval, baseline, readiness, conformance, technology mandate, or action authority

concerns.statement: The native hosts must share one governed engine and workspace-store authority boundary without inventing host-local Product semantics.

elements.name: GAEP governed engine
elements.responsibility: Own contract validation, immutable versioning, audit events, assessments, and privacy-safe projections for the bounded Product workflow.

technology.rationale: The current Product contract requires all native hosts to delegate governed Product semantics to one shared local engine boundary.

elements.name: Native Product Studio host
elements.responsibility: Collect explicit human inputs and render privacy-safe engine projections without synthesizing Product decisions or approval authority.
boundaries: No implicit approval or readiness transition

technology.rationale: Each supported IDE requires a candidate native adapter while the shared engine retains the authoritative Product behavior.

elements.name: Governed workspace store
elements.responsibility: Persist versioned Product-domain records, exact immutable history, transactions, and audit-chain evidence inside the selected workspace.

technology.rationale: The existing governed repository format is the exact compatibility constraint for this candidate architecture revision.

relations.interactionStyle: The engine performs lock-protected mutation commits through one repository transaction boundary.
relations.contract: Every mutation validates the exact contract, writes current and immutable-history records, and appends an attributable audit event.
relations.failureBehavior: Validation, binding, history, lock, or audit failure aborts the candidate mutation without a partial authoritative write.

relations.interactionStyle: The native host uses a strict versioned request and privacy-safe response contract over a bounded local process channel.
relations.contract: Unexpected fields, protocol downgrade, substituted bindings, digest drift, and private response fields fail closed.
relations.failureBehavior: The host reports a bounded non-authorizing error and exposes no private engine response details.

qualityAttributes.source: An accountable reviewer or deterministic workspace-health gate
qualityAttributes.stimulus: A governed System/Solution Architecture mutation or read is requested while the audit chain is missing or invalid.
qualityAttributes.environment: The selected local workspace contains initialized GAEP state and the current Product Initiative.
qualityAttributes.response: The engine refuses semantic mutation or projection and returns a bounded integrity failure without repairing authority-bearing state automatically.
qualityAttributes.measure: Zero governed mutations or trusted semantic projections are produced after audit-chain verification fails.
qualityAttributes.target: Every hostile audit-chain fixture fails closed before any System/Solution Architecture commit or authoritative projection.
qualityAttributes.verificationApproach: Exercise deterministic corrupted-chain fixtures and verify no current, history, transaction, or audit record is partially created.

qualityAttributes.source: A native Product Studio user reading one exact Initiative architecture projection
qualityAttributes.stimulus: A host receives a response with a substituted Product binding, changed snapshot digest, or undeclared private field.
qualityAttributes.environment: A supported local host invokes the strict protocol-v2 System/Solution Architecture snapshot method.
qualityAttributes.response: The host rejects the response and exposes only a bounded non-authorizing error without private payload details.
qualityAttributes.measure: All substituted-binding, digest-drift, and private-field fixtures are rejected across each implemented host parser.
qualityAttributes.target: Three hostile response classes fail closed in every supported native host implementation.
qualityAttributes.verificationApproach: Run deterministic host-client fixtures and verify exact response-shape, digest, binding, and privacy checks.

decisions.title: Candidate shared governed engine boundary

options.statement: Each native host implements and persists its own Product semantics independently.
tradeoffs: Four semantic implementations can drift and require separate authority-bearing migration paths
risks: Host-specific behavior may silently contradict the shared Product contract

options.statement: Every native host delegates Product semantics and governed persistence to one shared engine contract.
tradeoffs: Host adapters depend on strict shared protocol compatibility
risks: A shared-engine defect can affect every host and therefore requires broad contract evidence

decisions.rationale: The shared governed engine is the current evidence-backed candidate because it centralizes validation, audit, history, and authority boundaries.
assumptions: Each native host can launch or connect to the exact packaged engine build
consequences: Host parsers must reject response drift
Shared protocol evolution requires compatibility evidence
invalidationTriggers: A supported host cannot satisfy the shared engine protocol
The governed repository boundary changes materially

views.title: Governed Product Studio system context candidate
views.scope: The candidate view covers the native host, shared engine, governed workspace store, exact interactions, and bounded failure behavior.
regenerationTriggers: Host protocol or shared-engine packaging changes

conformanceCriteria.statement: Every supported host delegates governed Product semantics to the exact shared engine and rejects substituted or private projection responses.
conformanceCriteria.method: Run shared contract, engine lifecycle, controlled portability, host parser, packaged workflow, and conformance-matrix gates.
conformanceCriteria.evidenceExpectation: Exact passing receipts identify source revisions, package digests, host checks, known limitations, and zero synthesized acceptance authority.

lifecycleConsequences.statement: Protocol and governed-record changes require explicit backward-compatibility analysis for every supported native host and portable store.
lifecycleConsequences.rationale: Cross-host semantic parity depends on strict compatible request, response, and persisted-record contracts.

lifecycleConsequences.statement: Architecture-significant engine, host, or repository changes require a superseding candidate architecture revision and refreshed evidence.
lifecycleConsequences.rationale: The candidate must remain tied to exact current constraints instead of becoming an unversioned timeless diagram.

lifecycleConsequences.statement: Persisted schema or host-protocol migration requires explicit compatibility, integrity, rollback, and hostile-fixture evidence before adoption.
lifecycleConsequences.rationale: Automatic inference or partial migration could alter governed meaning or fabricate authority-bearing state.

lifecycleConsequences.statement: Interrupted governed mutations must preserve the last complete current and history state and expose attributable recovery diagnostics.
lifecycleConsequences.rationale: The Product Owner requires durable continuation without partial authority-bearing state after interruption.

lifecycleConsequences.statement: A retired architecture candidate remains in immutable history and is replaced only by a traceable superseding revision or separately governed disposition.
lifecycleConsequences.rationale: Historical design context must remain reconstructable without treating retirement as deletion or approval withdrawal.
triggers: The Initiative is cancelled or completed

governance.basis: The candidate owner and reviewers may prepare and challenge the design, but only a separate accountable human decision can approve an exact architecture set.

limitations: No realistic Product Owner architecture approval, implementation conformance, readiness, or release authority is represented
